The '''HP-30''' or '''Spice series''' are [[Reverse Polish Notation|RPN]] scientific hand-held calculators introduced by [[Hewlett-Packard]] in 1978. Some models are programmable. 
[[File:HP 32E calculator - pi in display.jpg|thumb|The HP-32E]]

==Overview==
Perhaps the HP-30 series, Spice, was to be released as a replacement for the aging HP-20 series.<ref name="HP30tech" /><ref name="HP-museum-38C" /> It has no expandability. The display provided better readability by increasing the digit size and adding commas.

The entry-level models were the HP-31E and 32E, which were not programmable, but even the 31E provided a self-check function.<ref name="HP-museum-31E" />

The HP-37E and 38E/C were the financial models of the Spice series.

The battery of these calculators can be changed without using tools. The housing is closed by screws.<ref name="thimet_HP-Models" />

===Programming===
The HP-33E/C (49 steps plus subroutines),<ref name="HP-museum-33E" /> HP-34C (70 steps)<ref name="thimet_HP34C" /> and 38E/C (99 steps)<ref name="HP-museum-38C" /> are programmable. The C-suffixed models have a [[continuous memory]].

The production of the 31E ended in 1980,<ref name="thimet_HP31E" /> production of the other Spice models ended in 1983.<ref name="thimet_HP34C" /> This calculator is well regarded in terms of quality, key stroke feel and daily usability for engineers.

== Simulators and emulators==
* [https://github.com/mike632t/x11-calc HP Calculator emulators]  for Linux

==Features==
* All basic scientific [[Function (mathematics)|functions]]
* [[Statistics]] (HP-32E,<ref name="HP-museum-32E" /> HP-37E,<ref name="HP-museum-37E" /> HP-38E/C<ref name="HP-museum-38C" />)
* Numerical integration (HP-34C)
* Programmability (keystroke programming with [[Branch (computer science)|branching]], [[Control flow#Loops|loops]], tests and flags)
